sections.h2: Your choices for selling a Pittsburgh house
sections.html:
Pittsburgh sellers usually weigh three paths: an agent listing, a sale by owner, or a purchase for cash. A listing reaches the most shoppers but leans on showings and a buyer's financing. A cash buyer takes the property in whatever condition it is in and can often close on a date you pick, which helps when the roof leaks, the stairs are failing or an estate wants out quickly.

Three local facts shape every path. The city doesn't demand a Certificate of Occupancy at sale, Allegheny County gathers the transfer tax at recording, and school tax on the city bill has its own collection rules. Sorting them out early keeps the closing date from slipping, and it tells you what the sale will really put in your pocket.

  • Find out who holds title and whether a mortgage or lien must be cleared from the proceeds.
  • Look up the Certificate of Occupancy record on the city's online search.
  • Have the settlement agent total the transfer tax before you agree to a price.

sections.h2: Transfer tax on a Pittsburgh sale
sections.html:
A sale inside the city carries a 5% realty transfer tax in most cases: 1% to the Commonwealth, 3% to the city and 1% to the Pittsburgh School District. Allegheny County collects it for all three when the deed goes on record, and it is paid by a separate check from the recording fees. Residential deeds recorded from February 1, 2020 onward carry the city's full 5%.

Part of the city lies in the Baldwin-Whitehall School District, where the school share is one half of one percent instead of 1%, so addresses there total 4.5%. The county's rate table lists each school district, so match your parcel to the right line before you estimate your proceeds.

The sales agreement states who pays. Transfers between close family members may need only a statement on the deed describing the relationship, while other exemptions need the state's Statement of Value form.

Pittsburgh doesn't require a Certificate of Occupancy to sell or buy a property, unlike many municipalities around it. That doesn't mean a property meets every zoning and building code, and many older single-family homes have no certificate on file because past rules didn't call for one.

A buyer may have to apply for an Occupancy Permit if the use of the building differs from the use on the latest certificate. The city tells parties to complete a Zoning Certificate request so the transaction meets Pennsylvania law. The most recent certificate is the current legal use, and two certificates can together cover a building approved in stages.

  • Search the Permits, Licenses, and Inspections online occupancy tool by address, parcel number, permit number or ward.
  • If a certificate should exist but doesn't appear, email the records office and expect a reply within five business days.
  • If you hold a certificate that is missing from the city's files, send a copy so it is added to the library.

Pittsburgh had 302,971 residents in 2020 and an estimate of 307,632 for July 2025, a gain of 1.5%. The city is divided into 90 neighborhoods, and the terrain is hilly: many streets are steep two-lane roads, and the city keeps about 800 sets of public stairways. Buyers pay attention to slope, drainage and retaining walls.

  • The middle home value among owners is $205,800 in the 2020 to 2024 figures.
  • Only 47.7% of households own, so more rent than own.
  • Median rent is $1,261 across 138,188 households.

sections.h2: Property taxes a seller must settle
sections.html:
The city, the parks fund, the Carnegie Library and the Pittsburgh School District all bill on the value set by the Allegheny County Office of Property Assessments. County values follow a base year of 2012, so the assessed figure is not a current market price. Bills go out in January, the full amount is due at the end of February, and a 2% discount applies for early payment. Installments fall at the end of February, April and July.

If you owe tax from earlier years, the city keeps past-due city, library and parks tax, while past-due school tax sits with Jordan Tax Service, Inc. An unpaid balance can lead to a Treasurer's Sale. Ask the Department of Finance and the collector for payoff figures before closing, since both come out of the proceeds.

The homestead program reduces the taxable value of an owner-occupied home. The city's reduction is $15,000, worth $120.90 a year in city tax, and a county homestead application also activates the city, school and library exemptions. A buyer who will live in the house should apply through the county.

Assessment appeals follow an annual window that opens July 1 and closes in early September. Check the county's real estate portal for the exact dates.

Under Title 68, Chapter 73 of the state code, you hand the buyer a signed, dated statement of known defects before anyone signs the agreement of transfer. Its subjects include additions and remodeling, water and sewer service, and land features such as sinkholes, drainage and flood risk indicators. Because of the city's slopes, take extra care with the land and drainage lines.

No special investigation is required, but a false statement is not allowed. A change in the facts before settlement must be passed to the buyer, a condominium seller covers only the unit, and a fiduciary selling for an estate is exempt from the chapter.

sections.h2: Work out your net before agreeing to a price
sections.html:
Take the offer, then subtract the 5% or 4.5% transfer tax if you pay it, recording fees, any mortgage payoff, unpaid tax and the repairs a buyer will ask for. The result is the number to compare across a listing, a sale by owner and a cash bid.

  • Is the parcel in the city, or in a nearby borough with a lower rate?
  • Does the certificate on file match how the house is used?
  • Are the city, library, parks and school installments current?
  • Whose name is on the deed, and does probate or a payoff come first?

A cash sale skips the buyer's loan approval and appraisal. At closing the deed is signed, the county records it with the transfer tax, and the title company pays off tax balances and your mortgage before sending you the rest.

faqs.q: Is a Certificate of Occupancy needed for a Pittsburgh sale?
faqs.a: No. The city doesn't require one at sale. A buyer may still need an Occupancy Permit when the intended use differs from the last certificate, and the city points parties to a Zoning Certificate request.

faqs.q: How big is the transfer tax inside Pittsburgh?
faqs.a: Five percent for most addresses: 1% state, 3% city, 1% Pittsburgh School District. Part of the city sits in the Baldwin-Whitehall district, whose half-percent share brings the total to 4.5%. The county takes payment when the deed is filed.

faqs.q: When do Pittsburgh property tax payments fall due?
faqs.a: The full bill is due at the end of February, with installments at the end of February, April and July. Early payment earns a 2% discount.

faqs.q: When can I contest my Allegheny County assessment?
faqs.a: During the annual window that opens July 1 and closes in early September. The county portal announces the exact dates if you believe the value is wrong.

faqs.q: Does my homestead exemption go with the house?
faqs.a: No. It ends with your ownership and the new owner applies. The city reduction is $15,000, and an application to the county also switches on the city, school district and library exemptions for a resident owner.
